# Individual Differences {#cognitive-section}

::: {style="text-align: center; color: var(--color-secondary); font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 700;"}
How do differences in the ability to control attention relate to cognition and well-being?
:::

::: {.profile-section-card}
People differ in their ability to pay attention, and those differences are a fundamental aspect of human cognition. We study how well individuals can control their attention and how this ability influences their **perception**, **memory**, **reasoning**, and **well-being**.

<br>

The **measurement of attention control** forms a fundamental part of our research in this area. We study how to best measure attention control, including the development of new tasks and approaches to measuring attention control in the lab and in real-world contexts.

<br>

[View and Download Attention Tasks →](){.link-cta}

<br>

The ability to **sustain the control of attention over time** is a critical aspect of attention control. Using behavioral, physiological, and self-report measures, we examine how this ability varies across individuals and contexts.
:::

# Neural Mechanisms {#brain-section}

::: {style="text-align: center; color: var(--color-secondary); font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 700;"}
What are the neural mechanisms underlying the ability to control attention?
:::

::: {.profile-section-card}

A key focus of our research in this area is how the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine (LC-NE) system acts as a central hub for regulating attention and arousal, and how this system interacts with other brain networks to support the control of attention.

:::

# Mindfulness {#mindfulness-section}

::: {style="text-align: center; color: var(--color-secondary); font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 700;"}
How can mindfulness-related practice enhance our ability to pay attention, and how can that, in turn, improve our well-being and quality of life?
:::

::: {.profile-section-card}

Contemplative traditions across the world have long emphasized the importance of attention in shaping the mind. We study how mindfulness-related practices can enhance our ability to pay attention, and that how that, in turn, can improve our well-being and quality of life.

:::
